title: Cozy Financial RPG & FinOS
author: Worried_Number5115
selftext:
My AI dev philosophy is to take my time to create a very good product instead of mass producing “ok” projects. Been working on this for 2.5 months so far and still have an incredibly long way to go but heres the current status (image & vid in the comments). 

To build the depth I want in the rpg, I may be working on this project for another 6-8 months. Do you ever feel like you’re dedicating too much time to a project? 

I’m in the process of a creating a cozy financial RPG layered into a personal finance education tool, budget tracker, & habit behavior tool recommended to a users specific situation (via onboarding questions, & optional manual account entry & or plaid linking) I got Plaid approval for all major banks and brokerages. 

The core loop of my app is a Financial RPG built into a financial operating system. 

1. Teach personal finance via bit sized and interactive 1-2 min lessons  
2. Truly gamify personal finance education via an integrated RPG that teaches personal finance through its gameplay and mechanics without lecturing. I have this in every layer of the game even down to the combat system where enemies represent “financial pitfalls” based on their mechanics.   
3. Recommend a daily “quest” which is a real life action & is a financial behavior change habit, such as checking if you are eligible for a HSA. I have a range of quests that have varying times & effort to complete  (daily v weekly v monthly quests) (3min v 15min v 30min to complete)   
4. Full Budget Tracking capability for a highly personalized and tailored system 

My game inspirations for the RPG are Fallout 4 (a personal fav), Zenonia 5, Stardew Valley, & The Oregon Trail. I took elements of game mechanics from these games while adding a unique spin and developing my own mechanics.

Let me know your thoughts so far. Would you use a gamified tool like this?

comments.body:
Hmm... This is something. I remember when YNAB was first making waves on Steam people were filing reviews as if it was a game... So... Umm yes! I like it.   
  
Financial literacy is NOT taught in schools and people find budgeting BORING.

Can I help?

replies.author: Worried_Number5115
replies.body:
Cheers, that’s a great idea and something I’m going to scope. This would add a ton of value IMO and personalize the experience more, which is ultimately my main goal. 

Some ways I’m personalizing it are having adaptive learning and habit recommendation based on a users starting experience with personal finance, wide ranging character customization, world building via user choices in life & in the game, & in game unlocks that require a real life quest to be completed, to name a few…..

Integrated localization is on my queue, thanks!
